By Mike Allen · Nov 05, 2026

Good Thursday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 658 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⚡️ Situational awareness: California Gov. Gavin Newsom moved to commute the sentences of all the state's 548 death row prisoners to life without parole. He told residents: "State-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us." Read the letter.
 
 
1 big thing: Dems shatter GOP statehouse control
 
Data: Axios research; Map: Andrew Pantazi/Axios

Democrats are on track to control most state legislative chambers, ending 16 years of Republican dominance over America's statehouses, Axios' Andrew Pantazi reports.

  • Tuesday's midterm results have dramatically expanded Democrats' power to increase minimum wages, protect abortion access and set voting rules ahead of 2028.

😳 Democrats are set to flip 12 legislative chambers, dismantle five Republican state trifectas (both statehouse chambers plus governorship), and shatter 11 GOP supermajorities, per AP.

  • If current leads hold, 75% of Americans will live in a state with a Democratic governor, and 53% will live in Democratic trifectas.

As it stands, Democrats will control the governor's office and both chambers in five of the seven 2024 presidential battlegrounds: Arizona, Michigan, Nevada, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin.

  • They have also broken Republican one-party rule in the sixth (Georgia) and flipped the House in the seventh (North Carolina).

🫏 Democrats flipped five GOP-held governorships (Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas) and lead in Alaska.

  • Republicans haven't flipped any, despite targeting Arizona, Michigan, Oregon and Wisconsin.
  • Kansas, where Democrat Cindy Holscher is leading by about half a point, remains uncalled.

The bottom line: Republicans spent 16 years building a statehouse majority. Democrats erased it in one night — and they now have two years to show voters what they'll do with it.

2. 🗳️ Trump: Sen. Sullivan should get other Sullivan's votes
 
Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios. Photo: Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call via Getty Images

President Trump said today that Alaska Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) should get the votes for Dan J. Sullivan, a candidate in Alaska's tumultuous Senate race with the same name as the incumbent, Axios' Avery Lotz reports.

🤳 Trump wrote on Truth Social: "The vote totals for the Fake Dan Sullivan, plus the other 'slug' that the Dems put on the Ballot, should be immediately given to the REAL Dan Sullivan, and the Election is over."

  • He added: "He easily wins. There is no other fair solution!"

Democrat Mary Peltola leads but Sen. Sullivan is close behind, with 78% of the vote counted.

  • The challenger Sullivan, who was listed on the ballot as "Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr.," is in last place with 3,600 votes.

📊 In Alaska's ranked-choice system, if no candidate gets more than half of voters' first-place votes, the last-place finisher is eliminated and their ballots are reallocated to voters' next choices until a candidate has a majority.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Data: Financial Modeling Prep; Chart: George Moriarty/Axios
  1. 😱 Tech stocks plunged today in the most visible sign yet that investors are growing worried about a slowdown in the AI boom. The Nasdaq was down about 5% as of midafternoon. Get the latest.
  2. 🗳️ Nithya Raman, a little-known L.A. City Council member backed by the Democratic Socialists of America, has defeated Mayor Karen Bass — an upset that will alter the trajectory of the nation's second largest city. Go deeper.
  3. 🚁 Drone delivery service Zipline raised $1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion valuation and expanded its Walmart partnership. More from Dan Primack.
  4. ⛳️ LIV Golf is officially shutting down, with attorneys telling a bankruptcy court that the PGA Tour rival would transition from restructuring to liquidation. Go deeper.
 
 
4. ⚽️ 1 sports thing: Ronaldo done with Portugal
 
Cristiano Ronaldo after Portugal's 1-0 loss to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Photo: Ryan Pierse/FIFA via Getty Images

Soccer legend Cristiano Ronaldo will no longer play for Portugal, ending an international career that spanned six World Cups, a European title and the men's all-time international scoring record.

  • His departure follows a high-profile falling-out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus.

🇵🇹 The 41-year-old Ronaldo said on Instagram: "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team."

  • "It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart."
